summary: A short walk among life-size dinosaur models headlined by a towering Rajasaurus, a kids' delight with a real Narmada-valley fossil hook.
description:
The Dino Trail plants a paleontological footnote in the campus: the Narmada valley is genuine dinosaur country, Rajasaurus narmadensis, an Indian predator, was described from fossils found in this river's basin, and the trail runs that fact through life-size models along a landscaped walk, crowned by a very large, very photographed Rajasaurus.

It is unapologetically a kids' stop: twenty to thirty minutes of roaring photo ops with signboards that smuggle in real science. With under-10s it earns its ticket; without them, it is a drive-past unless the fossil angle charms you.
highlights: Life-size models along a short walk
history_legend: Rajasaurus narmadensis, 'the regal reptile of the Narmada', was described in 2003 from fossils recovered in the Narmada basin, giving India its own named large predator and this trail its excuse.

seasonality.notes: Season-proof; shadeless at midday in summer.

experience.photography_notes: Shoot kids from low angles beside the Rajasaurus for maximum monster.

warnings: No climbing the models, enforced and sensible

emergency.nearest_hospital: Ekta Nagar facilities; Rajpipla civil hospital (~25 km)

tips: Bundle with the Nutrition Park for a kids' half-day
